information_source: Brand-Blinded product information (original brand information isolated)
scoring_basis: Dieter Rams Checklist & Eagle Eye Triggers (0-3 Scale)

verbatim_evidence: essentially the same pitch as the wave of clip-on recorders that came before it
1.1.reason: Reviewers call it a repeat of prior recorders.

verbatim_evidence: the transcription — the entire point of the device — garbled roughly a third of what was said
1.2.reason: Triggered: Core Flaw. Primary feature fails in groups.

verbatim_evidence: a bit anonymous-looking for something you wear on your chest all day
needed to retry pairing before the app recognised the pendant
All processing happens on the device — your conversations never leave your possession.
pulling the phone into airplane mode stopped summaries from ever appearing
1.5.reason: Triggered: Privacy Tension. Claims local, needs phone.

verbatim_evidence: after about four months the clasp loosens enough that it slides off a collar on its own
you have to open the companion app and leave it in the foreground before every session
2.1.reason: Adds a mandatory app step before every use.

verbatim_evidence: it needs charging every single night
2.2.reason: Nightly charging on a forget-about-it device.

verbatim_evidence: a second screen and a second radio strapped to a problem that a microphone already solved
2.3.reason: Described as over-engineered by one reviewer.

verbatim_evidence: most buyers already own two other devices that capture audio just as well
at $329 plus a subscription, you are paying flagship money for a feature whose accuracy nobody has been able to confirm
3.2.reason: Triggered: Price vs. Doubt. $329, accuracy unproven.

verbatim_evidence: if you stop paying the monthly plan, the pendant stops transcribing entirely and becomes an inert clip
3.3.reason: Triggered: Subscription Trap / Brick. Dead if unpaid.

verbatim_evidence: the free voice memo app already on your phone does the same recording and the same summary, immediately, for nothing
4.1.reason: Triggered: App Redundancy. Free phone app matches it.

verbatim_evidence: the audience for always-on personal recording remains a narrow slice of knowledge workers rather than a general market
4.2.reason: Serves a narrow niche, not a general need.

critical_issues: Triggered: Core Flaw. Transcription garbles ~1/3 of multi-speaker audio.
Triggered: Privacy Tension. Claims all-on-device but stops working when the phone is offline.
Triggered: Price vs. Doubt. $329 plus $19/month with unconfirmed core accuracy.
Triggered: Subscription Trap / Brick. Hardware stops transcribing if the plan lapses.
Triggered: App Redundancy. A free phone voice-memo app delivers the same output.

supports_toy: a satisfying click you'll fidget with

litmus_test_result.test: Does the data explicitly show the product causes more friction, expense, or privacy risk than the traditional alternative?
litmus_test_result.reason: A free phone app produces the same summary immediately, while the pendant adds a foreground-app step, nightly charging and a $19/month plan.
